problem: Find the equation of the downward-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(1,1)$ and which passes through the point $(-6,-6).$

feedback.problem: Find the equation of the upward-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(3,0)$ and which passes through the point $(-4,7).$
feedback.worked_solution:
For any upward or downward-opening parabola with its vertex at $(h,k),$ the general standard equation is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k).
$$

Here, the vertex has coordinates $(h,k)=(3,0).$ Substituting these into the general standard equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3)^{2} & =4p(y-0) \\ (x-3)^{2} & =4py.\end{aligned}
$$

We are left to find the value of $p.$ We know that the given parabola also passes through the point $(-4,7),$ so we can substitute $x=-4$ and $y=7$ into the standard equation and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3)^{2} & =4py \\ (-4-3)^{2} & =4p(7) \\ 49 & =28p \\ p & =\frac{7}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3)^{2} & =4py \\ (x-3)^{2} & =4(\frac{7}{4})y \\ (x-3)^{2} & =7y.\end{aligned}
$$
